There are some instances where an app offers better functionality. Consider apps like Boost if you still use reddit. Unlike the website, Boost has the following features:

  • no slow, jarring page transitions without animations

  • swipe to return to the previous page (like the subreddit you're on from a post) with no delay

  • night mode that's completely black in the background to save battery on AMOLED displays

  • multiple post browsing modes ranging from large cards, small cards, to a compact list of posts

  • all subs saved in an instantly accessible scrollable list on the side, no delay in accessing them

  • to type in a sub, you long press on the name of your current sub and then type in the sub name, no need to manually edit a URL

  • notifications for messages

Essentially, it's a faster and smoother experience that uses less battery and potentially less data, and I wish Voat had an equivalent. Granted, voat's mobile UI is better than reddit's.
